value.lineage: README: implements the 'Rapid Illumination of Behavior Space (RIBS)' framework; adopts the ask-tell interface from pycma ('Users of pycma will be familiar with the ask-tell interface (which pyribs adopted)'); 'We thank Amy K. Hoover and Julian Togelius for their contributions deriving the CMA-ME algorithm'; package skeleton from Cookiecutter audreyr/cookiecutter-pypackage. README 'Additional QD Libraries' names peers QDax, qdpy, sferes (not predecessors). Algorithms implemented and their sources are tabulated in docs/supported-algorithms.md (MAP-Elites Mouret 2015; CVT-MAP-Elites Vassiliades 2018; CMA-ME Fontaine 2020; CMA-MEGA/OMG-MEGA Fontaine 2021; CMA-MAE Fontaine 2023; DDS Lee 2024; DMS Tjanaka 2026; BOP-Elites Kent 2024; Novelty Search/NSLC Lehman 2011; QDAIF, QDHF). HISTORY.md tracks releases back through 0.x. || main loop (reader, from the code): The user loop calls Scheduler.ask(), which concatenates each emitter's ask() (GaussianEmitter: random archive elites plus Gaussian noise; EvolutionStrategyEmitter: samples from an internal CMA-ES), the user evaluates objectives and measures, then Scheduler.tell() inserts the batch into the archive (GridArchive.add: measure -> cell index, keep the per-cell argmax objective only if it exceeds the cell's threshold, returning a status/value add_info) and hands each emitter its slice of solutions and add_info so the emitter can rank, adapt its distribution and possibly restart from a sampled elite.

Focusing on this one commonly-occurring problem allows us to optimize the library for performance as well as ease of use.'
value.success_means: README does not state a numeric metric; it frames success as the three principles 'Simple', 'Flexible', 'Accessible' and the ability to 'compose a large number of QD algorithms' by interchanging archive/emitter/scheduler; the code tracks archive stats (ArchiveStats, QD score via qd_score_offset, ribs/archives/_cqd_score.py) and the examples visualise archive heatmaps.

organs.mechanism: a measure is binned as ((dims*(m - lower) + 1e-6) / interval) clipped; a candidate is admitted iff objective > cell threshold (strict; empty cells take threshold_min, default -inf); status 2 new, 1 improved; within a batch argmax wins (first on ties) and statuses are computed against the pre-batch archive

batch rule: ratio = (1 - lr)^k, new threshold = ratio*threshold + mean(objectives)*(1 - ratio) over the k admissible candidates of a cell; single rule threshold*(1 - lr) + objective*lr; lr = 1 (default) recovers MAP-Elites
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with lr < 1 a candidate between the threshold and the elite replaces the elite, so the archive's objective sum can fall

organs.mechanism: default ranker '2imp' sorts by (status, value) descending; with selection 'filter' only solutions that changed the archive are parents; CMA weights log(n+0.5) - log(i), normalised; restart from one uniformly sampled elite when CMA stops or nothing new was added
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: an empty archive makes the restart's sample_elites raise

organs.mechanism: ucb1 = success/selection + zeta*sqrt(log(sum of successes)/selection), zeta 0.05; never-selected emitters get inf; selection counts solutions emitted, success counts non-zero statuses; the plain Scheduler asks every emitter every iteration and does not choose
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the log uses total SUCCESSES (UCB1 uses total plays); all-zero successes give log(0) and NaN scores
